1. An Introduction to Large Language Mod.point: 预训练极其昂贵，微调让多数团队能在基础模型上低成本适配
1. An Introduction to Large Language Mod.core: It saves massive amounts of resources because the pretraining phase is quite costly and generally requires data and computing resources that are out of the reach of most people and organizations.
1. An Introduction to Large Language Mod.case: To create the Llama 2 family of models, for example, Meta used A100-80 GB GPUs. Assuming renting such a GPU would cost $1.50/hr, the total costs of creating these models would exceed $5,000,000!
1. An Introduction to Large Language Mod.explain: Meta训练Llama 2需A100-80GB GPU，按1.50美元/小时租金估算总成本超500万美元，说明预训练门槛极高；多数团队只能在此基础上微调适配。

2. Tokens and Embeddings.point: 分词器设计取决于训练目标，代码模型需要专门的分词器
2. Tokens and Embeddings.core: This comparison will show us that newer tokenizers have changed their behavior to improve model performance, and we’ll also see how specialized models (like code generation models, for example) often need specialized tokenizers.
2. Tokens and Embeddings.case: The GPT-4 tokenizer represents the four spaces as a single token. In fact, it has a specific token for every sequence of whitespaces up to a list of 83 whitespaces. The Python keyword elif has its own token in GPT-4. Both this and the previous point stem from the model’s focus on code in addition to natural language.
2. Tokens and Embeddings.explain: GPT-4 分词器把四个空格、最多83个连续空白各设为一个 token，并给 Python 关键字 elif 单独 token，说明面向代码的模型会定制分词规则以提升性能。

3. Looking Inside Large Language Models.point: KV 缓存避免重复计算，是生成提速的关键
3. Looking Inside Large Language Models.core: If we give the model the ability to cache the results of the previous calculation (especially some of the specific vectors in the attention mechanism), we no longer need to repeat the calculations of the previous streams.
3. Looking Inside Large Language Models.case: This comes out to 21.8 seconds. A dramatic difference. In fact, from a user experience standpoint, even the four-second generation time tends to be a long time to wait for a user that’s staring at a screen and waiting for an output from the model.
3. Looking Inside Large Language Models.explain: 同一提示下，开启缓存生成100个token仅4.5秒，关闭则需21.8秒，近5倍差距直观证明缓存省去重复计算、大幅提速。

4. Text Classification.point: 把标签写成描述句再做向量，没有标注也能零样本分类
4. Text Classification.core: We can describe our labels based on what they should represent. For example, a negative label for movie reviews can be described as “This is a negative movie review.”
4. Text Classification.case: An F1 score of 0.78 is quite impressive considering we did not use any labeled data at all! This just shows how versatile and useful embeddings are, especially if you are a bit creative with how they are used.
4. Text Classification.explain: 把负面标签描述为“This is a negative movie review.”并转成向量，与文本向量比相似度，完全不用标注数据就取得 F1 0.78，证明标签描述向量化可行。

5. Text Clustering and Topic Modeling.point: BERTopic 先聚类再从簇中提取关键词，给每簇一个可读主题
5. Text Clustering and Topic Modeling.core: BERTopic is a topic modeling technique that leverages clusters of semantically similar texts to extract various types of topic representations.
5. Text Clustering and Topic Modeling.case: For example, topic 0 contains the keywords “speech,” “asr,” and “recognition.” Based on these keywords, it seems that the topic is about automatic speech recognition (ASR).
5. Text Clustering and Topic Modeling.explain: 该案例展示 topic 0 的关键词为 speech、asr、recognition，据此可读出主题是自动语音识别，正说明从簇中提取关键词能生成可读主题。

6. Prompt Engineering.point: 思维链让模型先推理再作答，提升复杂问题表现
6. Prompt Engineering.core: Chain-of-thought aims to have the generative model “think” first rather than answering the question directly without any reasoning.
6. Prompt Engineering.case: The cafeteria started with 23 apples. They used 20 apples, so they had 23 - 20 = 3 apples left. Then they bought 6 more apples, so they now have 3 + 6 = 9 apples. The answer is 9. Note how the model doesn’t generate only the answer but provides an explanation before doing so.
6. Prompt Engineering.explain: 案例中模型没有直接给出答案，而是先写出23-20=3、3+6=9的推理步骤，再得出答案9，正体现“先思考后作答”的思维链。

7. Advanced Text Generation Techniques a.point: 窗口记忆只保留最近几轮，控制了长度但会遗忘早期信息
7. Advanced Text Generation Techniques a.core: Although this method reduces the size of the chat history, it can only retain the last few conversations, which is not ideal for lengthy conversations.
7. Advanced Text Generation Techniques a.caseTitle: 忘掉年龄的聊天机器人
7. Advanced Text Generation Techniques a.case: Now that we have added another conversation we are up to three conversations. Considering the memory only retains the last two conversations, our very first question is not remembered. Since we provided an age in our first interaction, we check whether the LLM indeed does not know the age anymore:
7. Advanced Text Generation Techniques a.explain: 案例中记忆仅保留最近两轮对话，于是第一轮提供的年龄信息不再被记住，直接印证窗口缓冲以遗忘早期内容换取上下文长度控制。

8. Semantic Search and Retrieval-Augment.point: 语义检索按含义匹配，能找到不含查询关键词的答案
8. Semantic Search and Retrieval-Augment.core: Notice that this wouldn’t have been possible if we were only doing keyword search because the top result did not include the same keywords in the query.
8. Semantic Search and Retrieval-Augment.case: Note that the first result does not really answer the question despite it sharing the word “science” with the query.
8. Semantic Search and Retrieval-Augment.explain: 关键词检索虽命中“science”一词，首条结果却只是影片简介，并未回答“科学有多精确”；语义检索按含义召回，才能找到真正相关的答案。

9. Multimodal Large Language Models.point: BLIP-2 只训练桥接模块，复用预训练视觉编码器与 LLM
9. Multimodal Large Language Models.explain: Q-Former 连接冻结的预训练图像编码器和 LLM，无需从头训练两端，只需训练这座桥即可实现看图说话。
9. Multimodal Large Language Models.core: By leveraging pretrained models, BLIP-2 only needs to train the bridge without needing to train the image encoder and LLM from scratch.
9. Multimodal Large Language Models.case: Instead of building the architecture from scratch, BLIP-2 bridges the vision-language gap by building a bridge, named the Querying Transformer (Q-Former), that connects a pretrained image encoder and a pretrained LLM.

10. Creating Text Embedding Models.point: 损失函数的选择会显著影响 embedding 模型的效果
10. Creating Text Embedding Models.core: A Pearson cosine score of 0.72 is a big improvement compared to the softmax loss example, which scored 0.59. This demonstrates the impact the loss function can have on performance.
10. Creating Text Embedding Models.case: Compared to our previously trained model with softmax loss (0.72), our model with MNR loss (0.80) seems to be much more accurate!
10. Creating Text Embedding Models.explain: 同一训练流程下，softmax 损失得 0.72，换成 MNR 损失后升到 0.80，说明损失函数直接决定模型精度。

11. Fine-Tuning Representation Models fo.point: SetFit 用极少标注就能接近全量数据的效果
11. Fine-Tuning Representation Models fo.core: Thus, this pipeline demonstrates the potential of taking the time to label just a few instances.
11. Fine-Tuning Representation Models fo.case: With only 32 labeled documents, we get an F1 score of 0.85. Considering that the model was trained on a tiny subset of the original data, this is very impressive!
11. Fine-Tuning Representation Models fo.explain: 仅用 32 条标注文档训练，SetFit 就取得 F1 0.85，接近用约 8500 条数据全量微调的水平，证明少样本方法能大幅降低标注成本。

12. Fine-Tuning Generation Models.point: LLM 权重矩阵内在维度低，LoRA 用低秩矩阵即可大幅减少可训练参数
12. Fine-Tuning Generation Models.core: This means that we can find small ranks that approximate even the massive matrices of an LLM.
12. Fine-Tuning Generation Models.case: A 175B model like GPT-3, for example, would have a weight matrix of 12,288 × 12,288 inside each of its 96 Transformer blocks. That’s 150 million parameters. If we can successfully adapt that matrix into rank 8, that would only require two 12,288 × 2 matrices resulting in 197K parameters per block.
12. Fine-Tuning Generation Models.explain: GPT-3 每块 12288×12288 权重约 1.5 亿参数，用秩 8 近似后每块仅约 19.7 万参数，直观证明低秩近似能极大压缩可训练参数。
